facts.name: Heart-leaved Aster
facts.notes: Clouds of small daisies that feed bees and migrating monarchs late in the year. Cut back by half in early June for a shorter, fuller plant.

sources.title: Black Cap Plants (Onekama, Michigan): Species list of native plants
sources.note: Michigan native nursery; marks the few species it sells that have no natural Michigan range (none of these are marked). Checked November 2026.

companions.why: Pair with fall aster, bugbane, eupatorium, goldenrod, sedum or toad lily; near bleeding heart; with variegated hosta and grasses.

companions.why: New Moon Nurseries: at a woods edge, try pairing zigzag goldenrod with heart-leaved aster (Aster cordifolius).
